correctness.rationale: Write E=A−I and F=B−I. The identity (K−I)BA=EF−FE shows rank directly. With t=0 at most one of EF,FE is nonzero, and K=I+EF−FE is identity or a rank-one square-zero update. Covector counts after imposing annihilation of the image line (and, when independent, both distinguished vectors), divided by q−1, give the stated identity and rank-one counts. For t≠0 the image plane has the simultaneous standard form E=e12, F=t e21 and splits off the common fixed space; explicit multiplication gives determinant one, trace 2+t² and nonzero off-diagonal entries, with det(K−I) on the plane equal to −t². The partner count is q^(2n−3) per t. In odd characteristic the conic (y−t)(y+t)=4 gives q−1 pairs, hence split-minus-irreducible count −2 on nonzero t and exactly the stated repeated cases. In characteristic 2 the Artin–Schreier equation has right side t^(−4), with absolute trace equal to that of t^(−1). In n=2 the t=0 nonidentity count is zero. Normalization by T gives the claimed limits; uniformity within GL classes is unconditional (the fixed-A probabilities are for similarity-invariant events only). Inspected the bundled finite checker and its recorded output; the all-field proof above does not use those tests.

evidence: When t=0, (AB−I)²=EF+FE and K−I=EF−FE. At most one summand is nonzero, so only the J3 product fiber maps to a nonidentity transvection; all other t=0 fibers map to identity. Its J3 count 2(q^(n−1)−q)q^(n−2) equals the frozen N_U, and the identity count is the remaining t=0 mass. When t≠0, the product trace determines t and the common two-dimensional transvection plane, after choosing a basis, has I+e12 and I+t e21. Thus the resulting trace 2+t² and nonscalar plane block give the class map explicitly.
